MindCompass — Adaptive AI Tutoring Agent

Capstone · Saudi Digital Academy & WeCloudData Agentic AI Engineering Bootcamp · Sep 2026 · Team of 4

An end-to-end tutoring agent that follows a continuous cycle: Understand → Plan → Teach → Test → Adapt → Remember. I designed and implemented the custom RAG module and co-developed the stateful LangGraph agent.

  • Built the RAG pipeline (PDF/Jupyter/HTML loaders, cleaning, chunking, OpenAI embeddings) on ChromaDB: 37 topics, 724 chunks, 0 ingestion failures.
  • Source-cited, topic-filtered retrieval via chunk metadata (course, chapter, lesson); manually verified results with top similarity scores of 0.57–0.67.
  • Co-developed the LangGraph tutor with a FastAPI backend (18 REST endpoints), Streamlit UI, PostgreSQL memory, 80% mastery-based adaptive paths and guardrails.
  • Validated with 37 passing Pytest tests and 12 end-to-end scenarios.

Majlis Amd — AMD Financial Council

AMD Hackathon 2026 · Generative AI for FinTech track · Solo entry

An on-premise, multi-agent social FinTech platform: three specialist advisors — Salman (savings planner), Noura (investment analyst) and Fahd (behavior and financing expert) — debate with a user or a group (travel, car purchase) and route questions dynamically.

  • Hybrid local-model architecture on Ollama (Qwen2.5-7B and Llama-3 8B): the right model for the right job, with zero cloud dependency for privacy and SAMA/SDAIA alignment.
  • Segregated RAG: a separate ChromaDB per agent, grounded in SAMA/CMA regulations to prevent context leakage.
  • Group governance: voting cards freeze withdrawals until all members approve. A secure tool sandbox with an anonymizing middleware sits between bank APIs and the agents.
  • FastAPI backend streaming tokens over SSE, with a message queue so the input never locks during council discussion.

FPGA-Based Brain-Computer Interface (BCI) Computer

Graduation project · Taif University · 2022–2023 · Supervised by Dr. Sameer Aoun Alsharif

A special-purpose computer that lets people play games using brain signals, aimed at accessible entertainment, including for people with special needs.

  • Designed a 32-bit pipelined MIPS processor from scratch in VHDL on a Spartan-3E FPGA; verified with instruction tests on LCD output.
  • Built a wireless EEG-controlled Flappy Bird game (VHDL, Basys 3, Bluetooth) with FIR filtering for real-time brain-signal classification.
  • Integrated general-purpose and special-purpose processors (SoC) for parallel signal processing and game execution.
